breakfast.name: Doro Wat (Ethiopian Spiced Chicken Stew)
breakfast.description: Rich and deeply flavored Ethiopian chicken stew made with slow-cooked onions and complex spice blend. Traditionally eaten for special occasions and weekends, often served on injera bread
instructions: Heat niter kibbeh in Dutch oven over medium-low heat
Add minced onions and cook covered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally
Onions should be very soft and golden (this step is essential)
Uncover, add ginger-garlic paste and berbere spice
Stir well and continue cooking covered for 20 minutes over low heat
Add chicken pieces and stir to coat with spice mixture
Add water and bring to simmer
Cook covered for 45-60 minutes until chicken is very tender
Add boiled eggs in last few minutes to warm through
Season with salt to taste
Serve on injera bread and eat with hands, using injera to scoop up stew
breakfast.notes: The long cooking of onions is crucial to developing complex flavor. Berbere spice blend is the soul of the dish
breakfast.fun_fact: Doro Wat is a rich, deeply flavored Ethiopian dish traditionally eaten for special occasions and weekends. The long cooking of onions develops the complex flavor
alternatives: Make with lamb instead of chicken
Make vegetarian with chickpeas and hard-boiled eggs

breakfast.name: Injera (Ethiopian Fermented Flatbread)
breakfast.description: Spongy Ethiopian flatbread made from teff flour with 2-4 day fermentation, creating characteristic tangy flavor and spongy texture. Serves as both plate and eating utensil
instructions: Mix teff flour with water to form smooth batter, eliminating lumps
Add salt and stir well
Cover bowl with clean cloth and leave to ferment at room temperature for 2-4 days
Stir batter occasionally during fermentation
Fermented batter should be slightly sour-smelling and thin, like crepe batter
Heat non-stick skillet or crepe maker to medium-high heat (do not oil)
Pour approximately 1 cup batter in center of pan
Immediately tilt and rotate pan so batter spreads into thin round
Reduce heat to medium and cook uncovered for 2-3 minutes
Top is set and small holes appear on surface (do not flip)
Transfer to large platter
Let cool slightly before adding toppings
Injera serves as both plate and eating utensil
breakfast.notes: The 2-4 day fermentation is crucial for flavor and texture. Injera made from teff flour, a grain indigenous to Ethiopia
breakfast.fun_fact: Injera is a spongy pancake made from teff flour indigenous to Ethiopia. Fermentation gives injera characteristic tangy flavor and spongy texture. Injera serves as plate and utensil
alternatives: Add spices to batter for flavored injera
Use sourdough starter instead of fermenting from scratch
Store in plastic for several days
